s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of a generalized eruption with fever and systemic involvement in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face
Large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
key_facts: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Patient was hospitalized 6 days prior for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
Temperature of 101.5°F
Normocytic anemia with hemoglobin of 11.7 g/dL
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 81 K/μL
Hypocomplementemia with C3 of 42 mg/dL and C4 of 3 mg/dL
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:1280 with speckled pattern
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
Negative hepatitis panel
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of SLE and current symptoms are consistent with a flare

shortlist.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was recently hospitalized for a photo-induced flare of ACLE and current skin lesions are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a generalized eruption with fever and systemic involvement, which are consistent with SJS

shortlist.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bullae and target lesions, which are consistent with this rare subtype of lupus

shortlist.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a severe skin eruption with fever and systemic involvement, which are consistent with TEN

raw.rationale: The patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus, recent photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, and presence of bullae and target lesions are consistent with bullous lupus erythematosus. The punch biopsy findings of dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, the current presentation is more specific to a cutaneous manifestation.

rejected.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient was recently hospitalized for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, but the current presentation includes bullae, which is more characteristic of bullous lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not include the typical mucosal involvement and widespread skin detachment seen in Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not include the widespread skin detachment and mucosal involvement characteristic of toxic epidermal necrolysis.
